criteria.required: Removing this paper makes at least one requested answer element (value, intermediate quantity used in a calculation, count, title, row of the requested table, or side of the requested comparison) underivable from the remaining gold set.
criteria.supportive: The paper's evidence reports the SAME class of quantity/design the question asks for, but for a system other than the one the question targets. A human can use it as contrast or confirmation; the requested answer does not depend on it.
criteria.irrelevant: The paper's evidence reports a different quantity/design class than the question asks for (different metric, different component, or no comparable value at all), so it contributes nothing to the requested answer.
criteria.uncertain: Question, answer, evidence text and locator together are insufficient to decide between required and not-required safely.
notes: Single-gold-paper queries are required by construction: the gold set has no other source for any answer element.
Figure / table / equation / algorithm / citation-count questions with an empty evidence_text_or_value stay required when the locator is what answers the question (rule 3).
Enumeration and per-method-row questions map every requested answer element to its own source paper (rule 4); no multi-paper query is collapsed onto one paper (rule 5).
task_family, primary_evidence_type, retrieval rankings, Recall scores and prediction files were not consulted (rules 8, 9).

evidence_used.evidence_text_or_value: To understand the underlying preferences of users and properties of items, various model-based approaches have been developed to learn hidden representations of both users and items (Koren et al., 2009; Xue et al., 2017; Rendle, 2010).

Recent
advancements in edge computing have provided a potential solution through federated learning (FL), which allows
users to collaboratively train models on their local devices
without exposing personal data (McMahan et al., 2017).

Despite its effectiveness in preserving privacy, the above paradigm suffers significant communication and computation overheads as it requires transmission of the full model and complete updates (Bonawitz et al., 2019)

Existing sparsityaware FL protocols reduce communication overhead at the cost of increased privacy leakage (Lin et al., 2022; Liu et al., 2023; Lu et al., 2023), as they inevitably reveal the coordinates of non-zero elements or significantly narrow the set of potential non-zero updates.
To mitigate this risk, secure aggregation (SecAgg) (Bonawitz et al., 2017) is adopted to prevent the server from inspecting individual updates during training
